claim: A local deformable-contact model with pressure distribution and sliding friction can be embedded in constrained real-time MPC and improve force/motion tracking on soft surfaces, but the experiments leave impedance predefined and therefore do not establish the value of online task-adaptive impedance selection.
epistemic_status: The model, constrained MPC, experiments, and limitations are author-reported; implications for minimal representation and adaptive impedance are bounded reader inferences.
problem_and_setting: Real-time force-modulated manipulation on deformable surfaces where simple spring-damper contact can mismatch distributed deformation, elasticity, pressure, friction, robot dynamics, and constraints.
method_or_mechanism: A spherical-tip Hertzian local deformation and pressure-distribution model with sliding friction is coupled to whole-body dynamics and solved using ADMM/DDP MPC with state, control, and contact constraints. Material properties are estimated beforehand; impedance is predefined.
content_summary: KUKA-EcoFlex experiments with force/torque ground truth cover static and moving surfaces and report improved force/motion tracking with force control. The model is local, restricted to a moderate force range, omits adhesion and rolling, and does not cover global deformation or lubricated/high-deformation friction. Online property estimation, richer contact, 3-D surfaces, and adaptive impedance remain future work.
synthesis_role: Direct closest-prior route for deformable-contact-aware constrained control that weakens novelty claims based only on inserting a richer contact law into MPC.
development_link: A new route must compare predefined and adaptive impedance while holding the contact-aware optimizer and constraints fixed, and test whether extra memory or finite-area state changes actions and held-out outcomes.

evidence.finding: The paper derives local Hertz-based deformation/pressure and sliding-friction contact, arguing simple spring-damper models mismatch deformation and elasticity.
The contact model is embedded with whole-body dynamics in ADMM/DDP MPC with explicit state, control, and contact constraints.
KUKA-EcoFlex experiments report improved force and motion tracking under static and moving-surface conditions.
The model is only locally valid; large bodies may require FEM, and high-deformation/lubricated friction needs extra modeled or learned factors.
Material properties are pre-estimated and impedance predefined; richer contact, online estimation, 3-D surfaces, and adaptive impedance remain open.

boundary_conditions: Local spherical-tip contact and moderate deformation only.
High deformation, lubrication, and global body mechanics are excluded.
assumptions: Local Hertzian contact is adequate in the tested range.
ADMM/DDP is fast enough for real time.
Predefined impedance is suitable across tested conditions.

reported: Simple spring-damper models mismatch the targeted contact mechanics.
Dynamic-surface tracking is worse than static.
The local model fails for large/global deformation and needs extensions for high-deformation or lubricated friction.
inferred: Model mismatch grows outside calibrated geometry, force, and friction regimes.
A richer model is not justified if it does not change actions or outcomes.
Nominal tracking gains do not establish safety under severe mismatch or contact transitions.

conflicts_with: Any claim that deformable-contact-aware constrained MPC is unexplored.
Any blanket claim that a scalar spring-damper model is always adequate.
Any claim that Hertzian contact alone solves complex soft scanning.
Any claim that this paper demonstrates optimal adaptive impedance.

problem_lead_search_contexts.lead_statement: The scientifically relevant extension of NNBO may be not merely replacing Hunt-Crossley, but determining when a richer contact state changes the optimal impedance action enough that contact-aware predictive or learned selection is required under bounded model error.
problem_lead_search_contexts.purpose: Test whether a deformable-contact-aware predictive controller is already a dominant closest-prior answer and whether its mechanism, assumptions, and outputs subsume the proposed richer-contact optimal-impedance problem.
problem_lead_search_contexts.expected_close_condition: Obtain decision-grade closest-prior evidence on model state, contact outputs, online feasibility, robustness to model error, and what remains unresolved for impedance selection in sliding soft contact.

problem_lead_search_contexts.lead_statement: The valuable question is to identify the minimal contact representation that changes and improves optimal impedance decisions in continuous soft sliding, rather than presupposing that an HC-pressure-field hybrid is the correct method.
problem_lead_search_contexts.purpose: Compare pressure-field, elastic-foundation, and other finite-area contact representations against the proposed HC-consistent distributed model, emphasizing which measured wrench components and geometries are actually needed rather than assuming a more complex model is better.
problem_lead_search_contexts.expected_close_condition: Define the minimum contact representation and negative controls needed to distinguish scalar HC, distributed foundation, pressure-field, and unnecessary high-fidelity alternatives in the target task.
